_what: KPI rollup across episodes (Stress Testing p6: KPI report). Flights recomputed from per-episode logs with guardrail.kpi.compute; stress bundles and sweep JSON as stored.

definitions.Family: one row per (scenario template, parameter cell) and Shield arm (Stress Testing p6). Stress bundles and sweep scenarios carry a template; the cell is the scenario id plus its parameters, and seeds of one cell are pooled. Flights carry no template: their family is rail / policy / mission, and the cell is whether the policy was hot-applied in flight and where a declared subject stood. AirSim follow flights of one policy share a row: they declare no cell.
definitions.P0 escape rate: P0 escapes / ticks, pooled over the family's ticks. An escape is a P0 violation still present in the action FLOWN (`emitted_violations`). Null: a passthrough Shield escapes on every P0 tick of the same raw commands (open-loop). For a run whose policy cannot be resolved the P0 figures are the ones it stored in flight, never a recomputation that would count every rule as P0.
definitions.Fail-safe correctness (ticks): ticks with a P0 violation on which the Shield acted / ticks with a P0 violation (the existing per-episode field, pooled). An always-brake Shield scores 1.0 here, so it is read with the next three.
definitions.Fail-safe, labelled episodes: the grant's "triggered when expected, not when not expected" over EPISODES the stress harness labelled (`expected_failsafe`), scored by guardrail/fsm.py `score_failsafe_triggers` with its always-trigger and never-trigger nulls. Where both this and the tick figure exist, this is the one that matches the grant's wording.
definitions.False triggers: ticks whose RAW action broke no rule at all on which the Shield newly braked or escalated (with the FSM's record: left Normal; a Brake held through T_recover is not a new trigger). A brake after a P1/P2 violation is permitted (Safety Shield p4, Normal -> Brake on violation), not false. A stateless Shield brakes only on a violation, so on today's logs this is structurally 0. n/m on stored tables.
definitions.Repair success: (converged + converged via ClearanceEscape) / (ticks with a repair attempt - ticks whose log cannot say). Failures: fell through to Brake / Loiter, escalated to RTL / Land (`fsm_state_after`), flew a still-violating action, or converged with a repair larger than theta (2.0 m lateral / 0.5 m vertical, Safety Shield p4). Theta is applied only where the log gives a size in metres (`magnitude_m`, or the FSM's `theta_exceeded`); no delivered log does, so every rate here is the Shield's re-check alone and is printed `(theta unchecked)`. `none attempted` = zero attempts; `shield off` = repairs logged on a control arm and never flown. Null: an always-brake Shield scores 0 %. No rail logs RTL/Land yet (WP3-07), so the fail-safe outcome is not instrumented.
definitions.Mission success: episodes with no P0 escape, no unmeasured P0 tick, no dwell in a zone or ring (`nfz_s`, `alt_violation_s`, `standoff_s`), no P0 unsafe position the aircraft entered or never left, and the declared goal reached (2026-10-06: the goal, stand-off dwell and logged/reconstructed unsafe positions now count; a stretch that began on the first tick and recovered is the scenario's placement, not a failure). Stored tables keep their own verdict with the goal re-applied. Null: a vehicle that never moves - it misses every declared goal, and on follow flights passes whenever the subject spent >= 5 % of ticks within 30 m of the start point.
definitions.Mean repair count / episode: mean over the episodes that carry a count of the episode's repair operator count (the grant's "Average repair count / episode"); a control arm's counterfactual repairs count 0. A passthrough Shield scores 0 - and escapes.
definitions.Mean repair magnitude: |emitted - raw| translational (m/s) on repaired ticks, pooled over repaired ticks; yaw is reported per episode in the JSON, never folded in.
definitions.Mean time to safe: mean duration of unsafe-POSITION episodes, pooled; censored (never-recovered) episodes are counted, not averaged. Logs without `unsafe` are reconstructed from the pose where the policy resolves; a dynamic (hot-applied) run cannot be and stays n/m.

headline: Repair success (Safety Shield KPI): 11713/11713 measured repair ticks converged across 47 shielded flights that attempted a repair (1196 more could not be measured: old logs without `emitted_violations`). Brake 0, residual violation 0, rescue heading 86, over theta 0. Null: an always-brake Shield scores 0 %. This is the Shield's OWN re-check finding the repaired action legal, NOT the grant's full test: theta ("magnitude < theta", 2.0 m / 0.5 m) could not be applied to 7660 of the converged ticks because no log gives a repair size in metres, and no rail logs RTL/Land (0 of 47 logs could record one).

How much that rate hangs on theta: under the velocity proxy (|dv| x horizon, guardrail/fsm.py), the converged theta-governed ticks that would be OVER theta are 0 of 7279 at a 0.1 s horizon; 5147 of 7279 at a 1 s horizon. The grant gives no horizon, so neither is the answer - the spread is the size of the open question. A further 381 converged ticks per horizon could not be sized by the proxy at all (320x velocity proxy on a tick with a kinematic clamp; 61x raw action exceeds the caps {'speed_max_mps': 3.0, 'climb_rate_max_mps': 1.5} but no Speed), and are in neither number.

Converged repairs flown while the POSITION was unsafe: 1264 ticks over 45 flights where `unsafe` is known (0 logged it in flight, 45 reconstructed, with the limits in their time-to-safe basis). A clean re-check of the action does not rule these out; they are the one independent look the logs allow.

Brake fired on 0 ticks in all 78 flown episodes. The Brake share of repair outcomes and the false-trigger count are therefore zeros of an event that never happened in these logs, not a tested 'no false alarm' (a stateless Shield cannot brake on a violation-free tick at all): the metrics' ability to see a brake is shown only by tests/test_kpi_magnitudes.py. Silence reads as success.
4 Shield-off control episodes logged repairs that were never flown (counterfactual). They read `shield off`, not a repair success of 0 %, and their repair count is 0.

Mission success needs the goal (Stress Testing): 4 sweep scenarios the stored sweep scored as successes never reached their goal and are failures here: `nfz-head-on`, `corridor-curfew-in-hours`, `standoff-reclassified`, `standoff-wedge`.

Mission success needs no P0 unsafe position (Stress Testing, "no_P0_violation"): 18 flights stored as successes spent time inside a P0 zone or ring they entered or never left, and fail here: `citylife_city`, `citylife_follow2`, `citylife_follow3`, `citylife_ped_0930`, `citylife_ped_final`, `citylife_ped_id`, `citylife_redcar_carpolicy`, `citylife_redcar_far`, `citylife_redcar_final1`, `citylife_redcar_final4`, `citylife_redcar_ground`, `citylife_redcar_pedpolicy` .... All are reconstructions, not logged verdicts: 10 against the single TRUE subject position (in flight the Shield had an estimate), and 8 against the NEAREST of several members of the subject class because the log does not say which one was tracked - an upper bound on the failure.

Hover null on follow flights: a vehicle that never left its start point would pass the follow test (>= 5 % of ticks within 30 m) on 54 of 60 follow flights, so a follow-flight mission success is not evidence of following.
`ros2_ped_off` time to safe: 0 unsafe episodes stored until 2026-10-06, 1 recomputed (mean 2.301 s); written back by tools/rescore_kpis.py. Cross-check: standoff_s rail 2.3 s vs reconstructed 2.3 s.
`sitl_ped_off` time to safe: 0 unsafe episodes stored until 2026-10-06, 1 recomputed (mean 3.562 s); written back by tools/rescore_kpis.py. Cross-check: standoff_s rail 3.3 s vs reconstructed 3.56 s.

`sitl_ped_side_off` time to safe: 0 unsafe episodes stored until 2026-10-06, 1 recomputed (mean 2.435 s); written back by tools/rescore_kpis.py. Cross-check: standoff_s rail 2.3 s vs reconstructed 2.44 s.
